chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Mubarak al-Aqarqufi, who said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, established zakat as a sustenance for the poor and as an increase for your wealth.'

key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islamic worship; here emphasized as a divinely ordained institution with dual purposes
key_terms.تَوْفِيراً: tawfir — multiplication, increase, augmentation; the idea that giving zakat causes one's wealth to grow rather than diminish
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Azza wa Jall — 'Mighty and Majestic,' a common honorific epithet for God emphasizing His power and transcendence
key_terms.قُوتاً: qut — sustenance, livelihood; the basic food/provision needed for survival

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah establish zakat according to Imam al-Kazim in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) provides a theological explanation for why God instituted zakat: it simultaneously fulfills the needs of the poor and spiritually and materially multiplies the wealth of those who pay it. This teaching was addressed to a companion who lived near Baghdad, and reflects the Imam's effort to help believers understand that zakat is not merely a charitable obligation but a divinely designed system of mutual benefit. The original audience would have understood 'tawfiran' (multiplication) as both a spiritual blessing — God's reward for generosity — and a worldly protection against the hoarding that corrupts wealth.
